$schema_note: Live measurements for the Mark 1 set (ForgePact#166 phase 1, research only, Live 1, Live 2 and Live 3, all 2026-10-13): how a bar slot can be cast through the game's own gate without a key press, which input entry each of Q, E, R and Y uses, what a toggle does under that lever, what a cast does to the walk, which script moves the player on a walk and during a jump, where a x0.5 on walking speed and a x3 on the jump land, and which reading tells a walkable landing point from one past the walkable map's edge. Research build of ForgePact 2feb9b4 (DLL SHA-256 0557663379cfbb08d1a976896f1b79712eae72dff47138e8f38194c08b02b97f; the plugin/ tree is unchanged at the head of the 166-mark1-set branch), the `mark1probe` instrument (nine script rows through HookOneScript, its levers and its pos sampler) and x64dbg hardware logpoints (CheckTalentUse as the control; TalentUseSetSpeed, StatMovementSpeed and StatJumpPower as candidates); save slot 14, character Sorak (White Mage), in Town_01_rm, every shipped mod off. Live 3 (walkability only) ran on a rebuilt research DLL, ForgePact 61243b2 (SHA-256 8c47459b15dd0691336efd65e5c9ded6ebd1a46b23e578e9688f71d023ad516e), with the same character, room and starting save and no debugger. mod_live_1 is phase 2's first session (2026-10-19, the walk's speed curve, the cast penalty, the toggle's settle time, the piece bases and a generated zone's edge), on the research build of ForgePact 109c908 (SHA-256 a2f64cf3889a4333e03c4fb0667045799b5fcb05f91e535c9fc171ff154ea493) with twenty rows (nine scripts and eleven builtins); its decisions are the research doc's Phase 2 decision keys. mod_live_2 is phase 2's second session (2026-10-19, the built set with its switch on), on the research build of ForgePact c598b5b (SHA-256 0a44a9d06ecd3780f1b4b4117e3178b4115f1094531e7869f368017c36b76362); its checks are the research doc's Mod live 2 results, and its 0.325 is a consistency observation, not a verdict. mod_live_3 is phase 2's third session (2026-10-20, the turn rule and the half walk with Healing Zone alone), on the research build of ForgePact 506038b (SHA-256 96c6d215ac87ab5e614b908abc937a404664b3aec60214a24a44c3401781483e); its checks are the research doc's Mod live 3 results, and it measured the 0.325 (penalty-stack: stacks). The procedures, their checks and the argument are in ForgePact docs/mark1-set-research.md (Live procedure 1, Live procedure 2, Results with Live 3 results, Decision, Not established); the shared facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md sections 7.7, 7.8, 19.10 and 19.11; the session captures forgepact-166-mark1-set-live-1.md, -live-2.md and -live-3.md stay with the hub's workorder files and are not tracked. No model or generator reads this file: tests/test_sdk_all.py checks only that curated/ is tracked, and the #166 workorder's criterion 24 reads game_build, cast_route, slot_keys, cast_penalty, walk_mover, speed_lever, jump_mover, jump_lever and walkable. A status is one of: measured, not-observed (the check ran, its control passed, and it saw nothing), not-run (the check did not run, or its control failed, so it says nothing) or static reading (read locally from the game, never measured). The decision value is the research doc's Decision key as recorded; each entry's checks carry their tools/live_checks.py verdicts. Addresses and call-site offsets are never recorded here; the callers are named. Static readings are our own words, never the game's text.

walk_mover.what: During a walk PlayerMovement runs once a frame, but none of the nine rows' calls changes the player's position: the walk's displacement is applied outside all of them. StatMovementSpeed runs once a frame standing or walking, every call returning to the dispatcher's direct call site in ReturnSpecificStat, and nothing called it directly.

speed_lever.what: x0.5 on id 64's result at the dispatcher, on every call for 240 frames, slowed the walk's step to 0.785 of itself, not 0.5. The lever scaled only the dispatcher's answer: skip=240 means every local StatMovementSpeed call inside the dispatcher returned a non-number to the probe, so the getter route never scaled (changed_getter 0), against the probe core's tested model. Halving the dispatcher's id-64 answer gave 0.785 of the step. Whether the step is not proportional to it (base, cap, floor), whether the walk also reads movement speed by a route the dispatcher lever does not reach (e.g. the cached pSt values PlayerMovement reads), and why the getter's own result was not a number to the probe (skip=240) are not established. The move lever did not run (instrument: no row moves the walk).
speed_lever.source: ForgePact docs/mark1-set-research.md (Live 2 results, Decision); forgepact-166-mark1-set-live-2.md (T6, T7), not tracked

ss_check.what: The draw's tier-5 test on protected value slot 75. A pushed SS stand-in is rarely built through the draw: 2 SS stand-ins built among 105 draw builds at magic find x10 (Live 1c), 0 among 6 at x1 (Live 1b; not pooled), against about 0.3 of draws expected if the draw kept the first entry it reads (s*c = 100 copies on lists of about 221 entries). Why SS stand-ins are rarely built is not established. The probe's picks= (47 in Live 1c, 13 in Live 1b) is an instrument count, not the draw's picks: it counts any CreateDefaultParams call in the draw's scope whose sub and b match a pushed triple read since the read window was last cleared, it does not compare the class, and a normal build does not clear the window. The debugger logpoint on the draw's own CreateDefaultParams call hit 105 times, equal to the 105 draw builds and including both stand-ins, so the other 45 counted calls ran at another call site; they are not the draw picking a stand-in and sending it back. Both slot-75 read sites were reached (at least 3.1 and 1.57 hits a call; the log condition's literals were read as hex, so counts resolve to 512) and every logged hit carried 75.0, a real, as the logpoint's logged value (139 lines). Whether that is the index argument or the value stored in slot 75 is not established, and the comparison after the read was not logged, so whether the tier-5 test rejects anything is not established either. No natural rarity-6 tier-5 unique was built through the draw in 28 minutes at x10; natural tier-5 draw builds came at k = 5 with rarity 7 (1, the owner calls it Angelic) and rarity 9 (2, Heroic). Aimbot.exe (class 10, base 76, rarity 6, tier 5) was built 8 times in scope outside.

mod_live_8.dropuniqueitems_on_kills: kill-calls 0 to 7 with draw-nested 0 to 7 in the owner's L4 play in The Devil's Breach: the ordinary unique roll ran 7 times inside a kill's DropItem call, over about 2900 outermost DropItem calls, and at copies 400 built Mark 1 Boots twice and Mark 1 Gloves once. What opened drop type 45's gate there is not established.
mod_live_8.hit_lines: No kill draw hit line, and no unique roll hit line for the kills' DropUniqueItems hits, reached bp_ipc out.txt; L6's by-name calls printed theirs in the command reply. Where a hit line made outside a command goes was not looked at.
